acceptance_criteria.requirement: No large selected-date details panel in any dashboard or preview composition.
No due-deck list or separate selected-date events column on the dashboard.
No dashboard Most Missed preview list.
A compact context bar follows both Month and Year legends.
The footer explicitly distinguishes Selected date, Event on this date, and the globally calculated Next event.
The event pencil opens the exact event editor.
Past and current dates expose Reviewed cards and disable it with an explanatory tooltip when no matching cards exist.
Future dates expose Due cards and disable it with an explanatory tooltip when due data is zero or unavailable.
Most missed appears only after at least one Again answer is confirmed.
Historical tooltips use Completed reviews and New cards studied; future tooltips use Reviews due and New cards due only when supported.
Month cells are 56 to 72 pixels high, or 44 to 52 pixels in the narrow layout.
Today, selection, focus, completion intensity, the quiet due band, and event diamonds remain visually distinct and composable.
Month due load uses a fixed narrow bottom band whose density and opacity distinguish low, medium, and high load.
Due-load normalization uses one robust p90 reference so a single outlier cannot flatten the forecast.
At 1320 pixels and wider, Month uses calendar left and the exact four statistic cards in a two-by-two grid on the right.
Intermediate layouts place the two-by-two statistic grid below the calendar; narrow layouts use one card per row.
Year remains full width with fixed square cells, visible month labels, and horizontal scrolling before cells become unusable.
The metric order is Today’s Progress, Today’s Session, Last 7 Days, and All Time, followed by the Bible verse.
Today’s progress is a count-derived four-segment workload bar; Buried remains outside it and Total remaining is the three queue counts.
New cards studied is used for historical counts and the Active days row is absent from All Time.
Large values use locale separators and tabular numerals; retention and Again-rate threshold colors respect opposite directions.
A stable page scrim and at least 91 percent opaque panel surfaces keep background imagery from interfering with text.
The Bible verse card is content-sized with balanced text and a clearly subordinate reference.
View, period, and settings controls have clear grouping, accessible icon names, focus rings, and responsive target sizes.
Tooltips remain inside the viewport without covering their target; Month has no horizontal overflow or clipped controls.
Calendar interactions use delegation, selection updates only changed cells, and statistics-only refreshes preserve the calendar DOM.
The layout refactor changes no study definition, saved preference, event, verse, or removed-component schema slot.
The 96-case theme, mode, view, layout, and scale matrix remains automated while VoiceOver and native Windows review remain explicit human gates.
